red_interpretation: The two short red vertical lines are the two pressed fold edges of a single centered box-pleat unit sewn into the middle of the yoke seam. Each red line is one fold edge flanking a flat center panel; they are construction folds in white fabric, not contrast fabric and not drawn lines. The red marks start at the yoke seam and extend only a short distance down (~9% of body length), meaning the folds are crisp at the top and release into soft fullness below — they are NOT pressed or stitched to the hem.
geometry_summary: Standard dress-shirt back with one horizontal yoke seam (dashed line, full width, at ~1/6 of body height below the shoulder line). Centered exactly on the center-back line, a box-pleat unit: a flat raised center panel approximately 4-5 cm wide (gap between fold lines = ~10.5% of yoke-seam width) bounded by two parallel vertical fold edges, one on each side, caught into the yoke seam. The fold edges are drawn only ~13px against a 144px yoke-to-hem body length, i.e. the creases are legible for roughly the top 8-10% of the back below the yoke, then the pleat fullness releases and falls as soft vertical drape to the curved hem. No darts anywhere, no additional seams, no stitch rows drawn along the folds, standard curved shirttail hem, plain sleeves/cuffs not the subject.
counts: Pleats: 1 box-pleat unit = exactly 2 visible fold edges (2 red lines). Darts: 0. Yoke seams: 1 (single horizontal dashed seam, full width). Other seams: standard armhole and side seams only; no extra vertical seams, no stitch rows drawn on the pleat.
